title: Personal-data flag: Data Classification v6 governs; default masking by classification
ruling: 1. **Source of truth.** DCPI v6 sheet Fields governs whether a field is personal, its category and its classification. `sys_fields.is_personal` = true exactly when the DCPI v6 row of the same field ID has Personal data = "Yes". 2. **Seed correction.** The data architect corrects the `is_personal` values of the PS v9 seed (staged, not yet released) to rule 1 before RWB-P1-E1001-APP is Done: 496 rows false → true and the four DF-DOC rows above true → false. LDM v11 sheet Fields follows the same flags. 3. **AC13.** RWB-P1-E1001-APP AC13 compares every baseline field ID present in DCPI v6: `is_personal` must equal (Personal data = "Yes"); any difference fails with the list of field IDs. A field ID absent from DCPI v6 is listed as "unclassified" and does not fail AC13; the 27 absent rows (DF-INT-030, DF-REF-274 to DF-REF-299) are **Pending, owner data protection officer**, NEW-GAP-E1; interim they are treated as not personal and the list is attached to the release evidence. 4. **Masking default (amends RD-P1-060 rule 2).** `FieldMasker.mask(dto, session)` (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) applies to every personal field. A field of classification **Restricted** (Direct identifier or Sensitive) with no unmasking rule for the caller is masked. A personal field of classification Confidential or Internal (Customer data, Indirect identifier, Staff identifier) is returned within the caller's case scope unless a masking rule masks it (DCPI v6 Handling and Key). Confirmation of this default by the data protection officer is **Pending**, NEW-GAP-E5; interim the FieldMasker fake applies rule 4 as written. 5. **RWB-P1-E1068-APP.** The guardrail reads "A Restricted field with no unmasking rule is never returned in clear". `personKey` and `contactKey` (Indirect identifier), `actorRef` (Staff identifier) and the promise fields `promiseAmount`, `promiseDate` (Customer data, Confidential; DF-INT-010) are returned within scope; `summary` keeps its own rule (masked unless the role may see it; RD-P1-072 rule 2). 6. **DP04 (GAP-3529).** No DP04 property is Restricted in DCPI v6; `contract_no` (DF-TRT-050) is Not personal, Internal, and is returned by permission. When the access-log entry of a records read cannot be written (RD-P1-091), the read answers **503 MSG-GEN-006** and returns no row (fail closed; RWB-P3-E1023-APP BR4 pattern). GAP-3529 is closed.

title: Temporal start mechanisms: client starts, child starts and Schedule starts
ruling: 1. **Client starts of AceIngestCheck** (readiness handler, fallback poll, admin): workflow ID `ace-ingest-check-{businessDate}`, `WorkflowIdConflictPolicy` USE_EXISTING, `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` ALLOW_DUPLICATE, unchanged. The admin rerun of a FAILED run keeps FAIL + ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY (Platform rules R22). 2. **Child starts** (`ReconciliationWorkflow` `recon-{businessDate}`, `Stage2ProductWorkflow` `stage2-dp04-{businessDate}`), issued by AceIngestCheck in the workflow task that commits the ALS stamp:    - `ChildWorkflowOptions`: the deterministic workflow ID, `ParentClosePolicy` ABANDON, `WorkflowIdReusePolicy` **ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY**, task queue `rwb-source-data`. No conflict policy is set (none exists for a child).    - The parent waits for the child's start promise (`Workflow.getWorkflowExecution(child)` in the Java SDK) before it completes or continues, so an ABANDONed child is never lost when the parent closes.    - When the start fails because the ID already exists (open run, or a closed COMPLETED run refused by the reuse policy), AceIngestCheck treats the child as started: it records nothing new, raises no failure and increments `rwb_source_data_duplicate_start_total` with label `workflow` = the child type. Any other start failure fails the workflow task and is retried by Temporal.    - A closed FAILED child is never restarted by the parent; it is rerun only through `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` (a client start with FAIL + ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY), or before wave 4 as in RD-P1-079 rule 4. 3. **Schedule starts.** Because a Schedule suffixes its workflow ID with the scheduled time, the Schedule `rwb-source-data-ace-late-check` does not start AceIngestCheck itself. Its action starts the short workflow **`AceLateCheckStart`** (task queue `rwb-source-data`, ID `ace-late-check-start` plus the Schedule suffix), whose one activity `startIngestForExpectedDate` computes the expected business date (RD-P1-041 item 1) and issues the client start of rule 1 with `startedBy` SCHEDULE. The fallback poll, when built (GAP-3277), uses the same starter with `startedBy` POLL. 4. **Catalog rows.** TWAC v3 R19 and R22 read "child start: deterministic ID, reuse ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY, already-started treated as started; no conflict policy (child starts have none); admin rerun FAIL + ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY". R18 keeps its policies. A new Workflows row `AceLateCheckStart` (P1, kind "Schedule starter", activity `startIngestForExpectedDate`) and a new Activities row are added; Schedules R12 reads "starts AceLateCheckStart, which starts or attaches to AceIngestCheck for the expected business date". 5. **Reuse rule (amends the RD-P1-040 reuse note).** "Every system-started workflow uses USE_EXISTING + ALLOW_DUPLICATE" applies to client starts only. In-service child starts use a deterministic ID, ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY and the already-started handling of rule 2. Schedule-started per-date work goes through a starter activity.

title: Readiness after the run closes, the readiness recorder and restarts before wave 4
ruling: 1. **XD-11 confirmed, with the mechanism.** On `POST /business-days/{date}/ready`:    - (a) a run `ace-ingest-check-{date}` is open → the client start (USE_EXISTING) attaches; answer 202 with the stored state;    - (b) no run is open and every due source of the date has its stamp row (`data_product_load` for the products it feeds) → nothing is started; answer 202 with the stored state;    - (c) no run is open and a due source is not stamped (never started, the run FAILED, or the run closed at 24 h) → a new run opens (ALLOW_DUPLICATE) and stamps only the missing sources; `job_run.run_no` + 1 when AD018 is live.    The check of (b) is the in-process `DailyCompletenessGate` source set of the date read by the handler. No second AceDataReady for a stamped source; no second ReconciliationWorkflow (RD-P1-078 rule 2). 2. **TWAC v3 R18** replaces "DONE or LATE starts nothing" with rule 1 (a)-(c). RD-P1-065 rule 3 reads with this rule. 3. **Readiness recorder (E1013-APP#1).** RWB-P1-E1013-APP builds the in-process component `ReadinessRecorder` with two methods, each idempotent and run inside the caller's transaction:    - `recordReceived(businessDate, startedBy)` – upsert on `uk_business_day_readiness`; first insert state RUNNING, `received_at` now. Called by the ready handler (HTTP) and by the first activity of every AceIngestCheck run started otherwise (SCHEDULE, POLL, ADMIN).    - `recordState(businessDate, DONE | LATE)` – called by RWB-P1-E1015-APP inside the `stampProducts` transaction that commits the ALS stamp (DONE) and inside the transaction that writes the ALS AceDataLate outbox row (LATE); sets `changed_at`. LATE may become DONE when ALS is stamped later; DONE never changes back.    RWB-P1-E1015-APP adds both calls to section 4 and its workflow contract; the E1015-CON workflow note names them. 4. **Restart before wave 4 (GAP-3390).** Until RWB-P1-AD018 is released:    - AceIngestCheck: rule 1 (c) is the restart: a repeated ready call (or the fallback poll where enabled) opens a new run for a date with an unstamped due source. The readiness row keeps its state until the new run writes DONE.    - A FAILED `ReconciliationWorkflow` or `Stage2ProductWorkflow`: the platform administrator (RW-PLATADM) starts the same workflow ID with the Temporal CLI under runbook entry "P1 run failed before wave 4", reuse policy ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY, input `{businessDate, startedBy: ADMIN}`, and records the action in the release record. A COMPLETED run is never restarted. From wave 4 the admin rerun of RD-P1-012 replaces the runbook step.    GAP-3390 is closed by this rule.

title: Flag-off answers: freshness never 404; 404 MSG-P4-003 for other flagged operations
ruling: 1. **Freshness and readiness never answer 404 because of a flag.** For `rwb.dataengine.freshness-stamp` off – before the ACE dependency gate and after a first-release rollback alike – `GET /data-products/freshness` answers 200 with every product `businessDate` null, status STALE (RD-P1-043 item 3(c), RD-P1-062); `GET /business-days/{date}/status` answers LATE for a date with a readiness row (404 MSG-P4-003 only for a date with no row, RD-P1-020 F); `POST /business-days/{date}/ready` answers 202 and records the readiness row (RD-P1-079 rule 3) but **starts no AceIngestCheck** while the flag is off, so no run queues while the worker is at zero. AceIngestCheck keeps its own guard (RWB-P1-E1015-APP AC40: a run that starts with the flag off writes no stamp, event or child). 2. **Other flagged operations.** An operation behind a flag with no flag-off answer ruled in an RD-P1 decision answers **404 MSG-P4-003** while its flag is off (the YAML form already used for the job monitor and the reconciliation results). Reads whose flag-off answer is ruled keep it: `GET /proof-of-delivery` (200, no row, DP07 STALE). 3. **First-release rollback (amends RD-P1-045 item 4).** Flag off; worker scaled to zero; the release's Schedules paused; operations answer as in rules 1 and 2. RWB-P1-E1015-OPS AC21 reads "the readiness and freshness operations answer as in AC5 and every other flagged operation of the release answers 404 MSG-P4-003". 4. **Ledger-writer flag (GAP-3506).** `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer` gates the REST append path only (404 MSG-P4-003). In-process callers are gated by their own flags: `rwb.dataengine.ledger-events` (intake consumers paused, RWB-P1-E1067-APP), the DM005 cutover switch (RWB-P1-DM005-APP), RWB-P1-E2034-APP's own flag. GAP-3506 is closed.

title: ON_CHANGE products and the DP04 stamp; active-count check; DP04 record selection
ruling: 1. **STALE by time applies to DAILY and WEEKLY products only.** RD-P1-041 item 4's `expected_by` trigger never runs for a product whose `refresh_cycle` is ON_CHANGE (DP03, DP04). The FAILED trigger still applies to an ON_CHANGE product that has a mapped source. The "Closes GAP-0511 (DP04: STALE at expected_by 08:00 …)" line of RD-P1-041 now reads "GAP-0511 closed by RD-P1-068: DP04 is ON_CHANGE and never STALE by time". 2. **One stamp component.** `data_product_load` is written only by the stamp component of RWB-P1-E1015-APP (`FreshnessStampWriter`, in process). `stampProducts` (AceIngestCheck) calls it for products whose `refresh_cycle` is DAILY or WEEKLY and that have at least one `data_product_source` row; it never stamps an ON_CHANGE product. `stampDp04` (Stage2ProductWorkflow, RWB-P1-E2010-APP) is the only caller that stamps DP04. GAP-3525 is closed. 3. **When DP04 is stamped (amends RD-P1-068 rule 6).** Stage2ProductWorkflow for D starts as a child in the workflow task that commits the ALS stamp (TWAC v3 R22). `stampDp04` writes the DP04 row for D (status LOADED, `source_system` `WORKBENCH`, `source_extracted_at` = the ALS `completed_at` of D, `loaded_at` = write instant) after every DP04 page of D is committed. When the core-bank code of ASM-5695 is confirmed and a DP04 `data_product_source` row is seeded, Stage2ProductWorkflow waits (durable timer, `ingest.poll.interval.minutes`) for that source to be COMPLETED for D before `stampDp04`; until then it does not wait. 4. **Active-count check (GAP-3524).** The comparable population is: for each `treatment_id`, the `dp_treatment` row with the greatest `business_date` ≤ D, counted when its state is active. Active states are the parameter row GAP-2696 names, **Pending, owner rwb-treatment owner with RW-COE** (GAP-3524 narrowed to the states). Interim: `checkActiveCount` runs in report mode – on a difference it lists the break with MSG-P1-002 and the count in the run result, but it does not hold `stampDp04`. The hold is switched on by the story change that closes GAP-3524. 5. **DP04 records read selection (E2010-APP#6, E2010-CON#7).** `GET /data-products/DP04/records?caseId=` answers, per `treatment_id` and per `guarantee_claim_id` of the case, the row with the greatest `business_date` ≤ the business date of the DP04 stamp in use. `recordId` = `treatment_id` or `guarantee_claim_id` (not the row `id`); `entity` = `dp_treatment` or `dp_guarantee_claim`. The contract number, contract date and plan terms are joined at request time from `v_ace_account` / `v_ace_plan` on the case's primary account: the `case_account` row with `is_primary` true and `linked_to` null, read through the rwb-case contract. Rows of a date later than the stamp in use (an unfinished or failed build) are never answered. 6. **Stories.** RWB-P1-E2010-APP, -CON and -OPS remove every "08:00 / expected_by / STALE from the expected-by time" statement for DP04 (s3, X3, s13, s19, AC4, AC5, BR4, s14; TC-P1-E2010-APP-08, TC-P1-E2010-CON-04, -12) and cite this decision; the E2010-OPS smoke asserts only that the DP04 row is written by `stampDp04` after the ALS stamp.

title: DP04 build reads, rerun and the records read value formats
ruling: 1. **Page base.** Every page of the Recovery Workbench REST contracts is zero-based (`page` minimum 0, default 0), as every published page in API Specification v7. The rwb-treatment read `GET /treatments?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size=` and the rwb-guarantee read `GET /guarantee-claims?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size=` take `page` from 0, `size` 1 to 1000 (default 1000 for the DP04 build), answer {items, window, page, size, total}, order `updated_at` then `id`, and answer 400 MSG-GEN-003 on an inverted window and 400 MSG-GEN-001 on a missing bound; an empty window [D, D+1) with no row answers 200 with `items` empty. RWB-S2-E2010-APP and RWB-S3-E2010-APP change "a page below one" to "a page below zero". 2. **Rerun and visibility (GAP-3523).** A FAILED run's committed pages stay; they are invisible because the records read answers only rows dated ≤ the DP04 stamp in use (RD-P1-081 rule 5) and a failed run writes no stamp. The rerun upserts by (`business_date`, record ID), then, before `stampDp04`, deletes the rows of business date D (both tables) whose `updated_at` is earlier than the rerun's start instant – the rows its answer no longer contains. GAP-3523 is closed. 3. **Value formats of `FieldValue.value` (records read, every product).** Timestamp: ISO 8601 with offset `+07:00` (Asia/Bangkok), seconds precision. Date: `yyyy-MM-dd`. Numeric: plain decimal string with the scale of the physical type (`numeric(18,2)` → `300000.50`), no grouping, `.` as separator. Boolean: `true` / `false`. Integer: decimal digits. A null column: the `FieldValue` is omitted. A masked field: `value` = the masked form, `masked` true. GAP-0512 and GAP-3528 are closed; GAP-3571 (physical types of uncast view columns) stays open for the ACE data owner but no longer blocks: the format follows the type the view returns. 4. **Order and total (GAP-3528).** Items ordered by `entity`, then `recordId`, ascending; `total` = number of `DataProductRecord` items over all pages (not field values).

title: Freshness stamp edge cases: missing batch row, re-completion, restatement detection, weekly-only sources, gate value
ruling: 1. **No batch row (GAP-3430).** In ASYNC 5.1.0 AceDataLate `data.status` becomes `type: [string, "null"]`, still required: the `v_ace_batch_status` value copied unchanged, **null when the source has no batch row for the date**; `completedAt` stays null. AceDataReady is unchanged (always a row). RWB-P1-E1015-APP AC41 and RWB-P1-E1015-CON AC17 and the sample assert `status: null`. GAP-3430 is closed. 2. **Re-completion of a STALE date (E1015-APP#2).** When (P, D) already has a row that went STALE (failed after completed) and every mapped source is COMPLETED again for D, the existing row is **updated in place**: status LOADED, `stale_flagged_at` null, `source_extracted_at` = the new latest `completed_at`, `loaded_at` = update instant, `duplicate_count` + 1, `version` + 1. No second AceDataReady, no child start (RD-P1-079 rule 1); the operations duplicate alert fires (restated batch runbook entry). RWB-P1-E1015-APP s4 step 7 and a new state row and AC state this. 3. **Restatement detection (GAP-3429).** While the run of D is open, a restatement is detected when the latest `completed_at` among P's sources differs from `source_extracted_at` of P's row for D (RD-P1-041 item 6 then applies). A restatement of a source whose new time stays below the product's latest time, and any restatement after the run has closed, is not detected by P1 in version 1. AC35 asserts the open-run case on the latest source. GAP-3429 stays open for the per-source store, **blocks build: No**. 4. **Weekly-only sources (GAP-3288).** A source that feeds only a WEEKLY product is due in the AceIngestCheck run whose start day in Asia/Bangkok is the product's cycle weekday (DP06: Monday, from `expected_by` MON 08:00), i.e. the run of the latest bank business day before that day. That run raises AceDataLate for the source at 05:30 of the cycle day with that business date and holds DP06's `expected_by` timer (MON 08:00). Other runs neither poll nor raise anything for the source. GAP-3288 is closed; confirmation of the cycle-day rule by the ACE team lead is recommended. 5. **Gate value over REST (GAP-3434).** No gate member is added to `GET /data-products/freshness`. `DailyCompletenessGate` is in-process only (`listEligibleAccounts`, `/efs-history`, reconciliation, AD019); a REST caller uses the per-product `status` and `GET /business-days/{date}/status`. RWB-P1-E1015-CON removes the REST gate assertion. GAP-3434 is closed.

title: Proof-of-delivery: incomplete WIN date and the contract publisher

title: Reconciliation results: REC-05 aggregate row, result page, alert values, rwb-case inputs
ruling: 1. **REC-05 is served as one aggregate row per business date** in `reconciliation_result`: `rec_code` REC-05, `product_group` `ALL`, `source_count` = keys checked, `workbench_count` = keys resolved, `variance_count` = orphan keys, `variance_pct` = orphans / keys checked × 100 (0 when none checked), `tolerance_pct` 0.0000, `result` PASS when `variance_count` = 0, else BREAK. The YAML `recCode` enum becomes [REC-01, REC-02, REC-05]; the LOV of `product_group` for results adds `ALL` (Reference Data and Lists of Values v6). title: Ledger writer refusals and the actor check
ruling: Nothing is written in any refusal. 1. **DECISION_TAKEN (GAP-3487).** No `decisionLogId` → 422 MSG-GEN-001, `field` decisionLogId. The decision-log read answers 404, or the entry's `caseId` is not the path case → 422 MSG-GEN-007, `field` decisionLogId. The read does not answer in 2 s or answers 503 → 503 MSG-P1-022 (as X6). GAP-3487 is closed. 2. **CORRECTION (GAP-3489).** `correctsEntryId` unknown or of another case → 422 MSG-GEN-007, `field` correctsEntryId. 3. **Future occurredAt (GAP-3489).** `occurredAt` later than the server receipt instant plus `ledger.occurred-at.future-tolerance.seconds` (values file, 300) → 422 MSG-GEN-003, `field` occurredAt. GAP-3489 is closed. 4. **Other service identities (GAP-3492).** A service identity other than rwb-case whose case read answers 404 or 403 gets 404 MSG-P4-003, as a user caller (X4). 5. **Actor check (GAP-3492).** For a delegated user token (a token with a user subject), `actorType` must be USER and `actorRef` must equal the token's Workbench user identifier; otherwise 403 MSG-P4-002. For a workload token, `actorType` and `actorRef` are stored as sent (the calling service vouches; RD-P1-009). GAP-3492 is closed; confirmation by compliance is recommended. 6. The provider fake of RWB-P1-E1066-CON s12.8 maps each of these refusals.

title: Ledger intake: refusals that are not transient
ruling: 1. Such a refusal is parked **at once** on `<topic>.dlt` (no retry topic), with `rwb-dlt-consumer=rwb-source-data`, `rwb-dlt-owner=P1 squad` and `rwb-dlt-reason`:    - `CASE_NOT_FOUND` – the case read answers 404 or 403;    - `VALIDATION_REFUSED` – the writer answers 422 (any field), the field name in header `rwb-dlt-field`;    - `DECISION_REF_REFUSED` – the DECISION_TAKEN reference is missing or refused (RD-P1-087 rule 1). 2. The offset is committed after the `.dlt` write; `processed_event` records the `ce_id` with no entry; no LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED is raised (it stays for RETRIES_EXHAUSTED). A decision-log or case read that does not answer stays transient (retry path). 3. Replay after correction uses the platform replay tool; the business key prevents a duplicate entry. 4. RWB-P1-E1067-APP X6 and AC8 read: "no entry; parked at once with `CASE_NOT_FOUND`; the consumer log shows the case ID and no payload value". RWB-P1-E1067-CON AC5, AC11 and the writer stub follow.
